findings.title: Background cites a publication that the saved prior art records as fictional
findings.attack: [0007] describes 'US2019/0123456A1'. The prior-art index lists that number only as requester item S1, marked as a fictional test reference that was never fetched. If a real document of that number exists, the description misstates it: a US duty-of-candour problem (37 CFR 1.56) and, at the EPO and UK, an admission that the listed features were known. Must be corrected before filing.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete [0007], or rewrite it without a publication number only if the inventor or counsel confirms the approaches are known. Recheck [0013] afterwards.

findings.title: Drawn captions call FIGS. 10, 11A-11C, 12A-12B and 13A candidate constructions shown for disclosure of the genus only
findings.attack: The figure instructions require captions on the sheets such as 'Candidate alternative seat-ring geometries; not built or tested; shown for disclosure of the genus only' and 'retained pending confirmation'. A drawing stating that the construction is a candidate pending confirmation invites a US written-description attack on possession of claims 26, 40-44, 66 and 67 and gives an opponent a quotation against reliance on those figures.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Remove 'Candidate', 'shown for disclosure of the genus only' and 'pending confirmation' from the drawn captions; keep the description's plain statements that no test was made. The human confirms conception at the gate; unconfirmed embodiments and their claims come out rather than being filed as candidates.

findings.title: Outward movement of the wall is said to open a gap to the surrounding bore in which the ring is interference fitted
findings.attack: Radial expansion is an outward movement of the wall, yet it is said to open a clearance between the wall and the bore around it, in which the ring is held with no clearance. The relief construction does not say how expansion breaks the closing line contact, and [0202] says it is not the tested construction, so the tested construction is undisclosed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add disclosure of the prototype construction at the outer surface of the seat ring: extent of the fit, clearance at rest, closing line, how expansion unseats it, entry and exit of the purge flow. No claim narrowing.

findings.title: Point of application, direction and conversion of the axial load are not disclosed and are stated inconsistently
findings.attack: No paragraph says where on the seat ring the purge shoulder bears, in which direction, or what reacts the load; [0113] places the load at the sealing edge, which the poppet has left in over-travel. [0134] and [0170] say the convolution flattens, [0172] says the bow increases, and [0237] derives a 0.15 mm gap from flattening a 0.12 mm convolution.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add disclosure from the prototype record of the contact surface, load direction, stress state of the wall and sense of each convolution; reconcile [0113], [0134], [0170], [0172] and [0237]. No claim narrowing.

findings.title: The axial load path through the seat ring is not described consistently
findings.attack: The load point, the reaction and the direction of wall movement are not stated, and the text conflicts: [0113] loads the upper (sealing) edge, FIG. 2 instructions load the fit-band end, [0167]/[0186] put the fit band at the end opposite the sealing edge, FIG. 1 instructions put both at the tyre-chamber end, and [0116] has the poppet moving away from the sealing edge. [0134], [0237] and claim 22 say the convolution flattens under the axial load, while [0172] says the equivalent bow increases under the same load. An examiner has a verifiable internal contradiction to raise sufficiency (EPO) and enablement/written description (US) against the principal embodiment.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add one paragraph from the built prototype stating which end of the seat ring faces the tyre chamber, where the purge shoulder bears, what surface of the core body reacts the load and how the convoluted wall moves; conform [0113], [0134], [0237], FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 instructions and claim 22. No claim narrowing needed.

findings.title: Two-piece seat has no disclosed purge gap although claim 1 reaches it through reference signs 142 and 146
findings.attack: Numeral 146 is absent from the description. The two-piece seat paragraphs and Statement 7.1 describe outward deflection and wiping only; no flow path, location, closed state or distinction from the main passage is stated.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0181]-[0183] and Statement 7.1 the purge gap 146, its boundaries, closed state at rest and flow path; then add a dependent claim to the two-piece seat.

findings.title: Claim 2 omits the pump head and pressure differential present in every description of the method
findings.attack: Every description of the method couples and removes a pump head and applies a pressure differential; no other way of moving the poppet is described and [0090] defines the inflation cycle by a pump head.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a paragraph and claim-support statement in the terms of claim 2, with any other means of moving the poppet the inventor conceived; revise [0090].

findings.title: Claim 24 dependent on claim 22 combines two contradictory statements
findings.attack: Claim 24 ('a single outward bow') may depend on claim 22 ('the axial load flattens the at least one convolution'); [0172] says 'The bow increases under axial load'. The combination is contradicted by the description.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Make claim 24 depend on claim 21 only, unless F-28-1 is resolved in a way that reconciles the two.

findings.title: Claim 4 claims shape-setting alone; every method passage includes laser cutting and quenching
findings.attack: Claim 4: 'shape-setting (512) the seat ring in a fixture that holds the load-converting geometry'. [0022], [0252] and statement 5.1 always present laser cutting, shape-setting and quenching together; standalone shape-setting appears only in the definition [0098].
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a sentence that the NiTi seat ring may be made by a method comprising the shape-setting, the other FIG. 7 steps being optional.

findings.title: Claim 79 laser cutting to a profile of the convoluted wall is not explained and conflicts with [0170] and [0254]
findings.attack: Claim 79: 'the laser cutting cuts the seat ring to a profile of the convoluted wall'. The convolution is a wave in the wall section; [0170] and [0254] say it is pressed in the shape-setting fixture and laser cutting only trims the ends. How a laser produces a sectional wave is not described.
findings.least_narrowing_action: State in [0253] what 'profile' means (for example the axial outline of the blank), or delete claim 79.

findings.title: Claimed combinations fall outside the combinations the description permits
findings.attack: [0035] and [0349] confine combinations to those set out under Combinations. Polymer seat ring with fit band and relief, polymer seat ring with hard-anodised sealing face, fit band without relief, and purge gap width for other elements are not set out.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Replace the closed wording of [0035] and [0349] with an open statement and add the specific combinations claimed.

findings.title: FIG. 1 instructions place the main passage against the core body bore
findings.attack: FIG. 1 instructions draw 'the main passage (26) as the annular flow path between the poppet (40) and the core body bore (22)', whereas [0123] and [0126] put it between the sealing edge and the sealing face, and the purge gap is bounded by the core body bore. The drawing blurs the distinction on which claim 1 rests.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Change the FIG. 1 instruction so that the lead line for 26 ends at the path between the sealing face 42 and the sealing edge 32.

findings.title: FIG. 13A and numerals 146 and 220 have no description
findings.attack: The figure plan and instructions include FIG. 13A (Schrader-pattern core body 220) and the registry lists 146 and 220; the brief description lists FIG. 13B alone and neither FIG. 13A, 146 nor 220 appears in the description. Claim 1 uses 146. Formal objections under EPO Rules 42(1)(d) and 46(2)(i) and 37 CFR 1.74 and 1.84(p)(5).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Describe FIG. 13A and purge gap 146, or remove FIG. 13A, renumber FIG. 13B as FIG. 13 and remove 146 and 220 from claims and registry.

findings.title: Figure files are instructions, carry drafting-process statements and number items the description does not describe
findings.attack: No drawing exists. The figure plan records FIGS. 11, 12 and 13A as not stated in the inventor's disclosure and the captions call them candidates, while the description calls them embodiments. Numerals 146, 220, 402, 404 and FIG. 13A are absent from the description.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Remove the drafting-process statements and captions; describe or remove FIG. 13A and numerals 146, 220, 402 and 404.

findings.title: Purge gap and closed state at rest not disclosed for the slotted sleeve, split seat ring and tapered seat ring
findings.attack: The slots of the slotted sleeve exist at rest and nothing closes them; the split seat ring paragraph does not identify the purge gap; the tapered seat ring paragraph describes none. None says where the sealing edge is.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add for each form the location of the purge gap, what closes it at rest and where the sealing edge is.

findings.title: Ranges and prototype values generalised from the seat ring to every radially deflectable element
findings.attack: Claims 19 ('a purge gap width of from 0.10 mm to 0.25 mm'), 33 and 34 depend on claim 1 without the seat ring. [0236] and [0237] state the ranges for the purge shoulder bearing on the seat ring 30 and for purge gap 60 opened by flattening of convolution 36; statement 1.23 attaches them only to the seat ring. No disclosure with the wiper ring, slotted sleeve, split or tapered seat ring; amendment of claim 1 with these ranges alone would be an intermediate generalisation.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If the inventor agrees, add a sentence that these ranges apply to each form of the radially deflectable element; otherwise make claims 19, 33 and 34 depend on claim 20, giving up the ranges for the other forms.

findings.title: Slotted sleeve, split seat ring and tapered seat ring: no closed-at-rest purge gap and no seal at rest described
findings.attack: Claim 1 requires a purge gap 'closed at rest and throughout the normal stroke' and a sealing face seated on a sealing edge. [0176] calls the axial slots a purge route when spread but never says they are closed at rest or whether the sleeve carries the sealing edge; [0177] does not say which path is the purge gap; [0178] says nothing of the purge gap or seal. The combination rests only on the general statement at [0163].
findings.least_narrowing_action: For each form add one sentence stating where the sealing edge is, which path is the purge gap and what closes it at rest and through the normal stroke, if within the inventor's conception.

findings.title: Snap-back wipe across the sealing face is claimed at a time when the sealing face is spaced from the seat ring
findings.attack: [0137] puts the shape recovery before the return through the normal stroke, so the sealing face is 0.6 mm from the sealing edge when the wipe is said to occur; [0138] offers the wipe as a belief. Claims 32 and 76 extend it to polymer seat rings, beyond Statement 1.20.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the inventor's account of when and where contact occurs; meanwhile restrict claims 32 and 76 to the superelastic seat ring claims, giving up a wipe claim for polymer seat rings.

findings.title: The snap-back wipe cannot occur in the sequence the description gives
findings.attack: Claims recite 'the seat ring moves across the sealing face of the poppet in a snap-back wipe'. [0137] has the seat ring recover and the purge gap close before 'The poppet 40 then returns through the normal stroke 114 and the sealing face 42 seats again', so the sealing face is at least a normal stroke away when the ring recovers. [0138] states the mechanism only as a belief.
findings.least_narrowing_action: State from the inventor's observation what surface the recovering seat ring moves across and when the sealing face contacts it; or recast claims 32, 56 and 76 to shape recovery of a superelastic seat ring on removal of the axial load.

findings.title: Two-piece seat: purge gap 146 and the route of the purge shoulder to the wiper ring are not described
findings.attack: Claim 1 recites 'a purge gap (60, 146)' and 'a sealing edge (32, 132, 142)'. Numeral 146 does not occur in the description; [0181]-[0183] and [0293]-[0295] never say the wiper ring deflection opens a purge gap, where it lies or that it is distinct from the main passage, nor how a purge shoulder below the sealing face reaches a wiper ring below the rigid seat.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0182] the location of purge gap 146, that it is distinct from the main passage 26, and the path by which the purge shoulder reaches the wiper ring.

findings.title: Claim 2 recites closing of the purge gap without the shape recovery the description pairs with it
findings.attack: Claim 2: 'so that the axial load is removed and the purge gap closes'. Every passage states the closing is by shape recovery; claim 2 is broader, a support weakness if read to cover closing by other means.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a sentence that the purge gap closes on removal of the axial load, by the shape recovery alone or assisted, for example by the garter spring of [0211].

findings.title: Claim 24 on claim 22 claims a bow that flattens where the description says it increases
findings.attack: [0172] says the bow increases under axial load; claim 22 requires the convolution to flatten.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Make claim 24 dependent on claim 21 only, or resolve under F-28-1.

findings.title: Claim 68 recites a convolution amplitude when it may depend on claim 3 alone
findings.attack: Claim 68 ('a convolution amplitude of from 0.08 mm to 0.20 mm') may depend on claim 3, which does not require a convolution; the load-converting geometry may be a strut pattern, helical slot or taper. Claim 69 likewise.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Make the convolution-amplitude alternative of claim 68 and all of claim 69 depend on claim 62.

findings.title: Claim 9 omits the stop and staggered engagement that produce the two rates
findings.attack: Series springs are disclosed with a stop and nested springs with staggered engagement; without them the arrangements give one rate.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a sentence that the stop and the staggered engagement are examples of means by which the second spring stage is engaged.

findings.title: Claims 12 and 34 isolate prototype values from the prototype
findings.attack: The values are disclosed as those of one built configuration, together with every other prototype value.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a sentence that each prototype value is disclosed independently of the others.

findings.title: Disclosed alternatives lie outside every claim, one by the description's own statement
findings.attack: [0179] describes a disc spring that opens a purge gap and says its deflection is not a radial expansion, which tells a competitor how to avoid claim 1. The detent and spring-loaded stop are outside claim 6. Unclaimed disclosed subject matter is dedicated to the public in the United States.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a generic claim to a deflectable element whose deflection opens the purge gap, with claim-support statements and a figure, and a generic term for the threshold-separating return arrangement. Nothing is given up.

findings.title: Two-piece seat cannot serve as a fallback because its purge gap is not described
findings.attack: An amendment to the rigid seat and wiper ring must state that the wiper ring's deflection opens the purge gap; the description says only that it deflects outward and wipes. The amendment would be refused as not directly and unambiguously disclosed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the purge gap 146 to the two-piece seat paragraphs and Statement 7.1: boundaries, closed state at rest, relation to the main passage, path of the air purge.

findings.title: Combination clause is closed
findings.attack: Features may be combined only in the combinations set out under Combinations, and [0217] lists six forms that exclude the slotted sleeve, split seat ring, tapered seat ring, collar, detent and wall slots.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Replace with an open statement and extend [0217] to every form of the radially deflectable element, load-applying surface and return bias.

findings.title: Example 1 does not state the convolution count, return-spring construction or purge-gap boundary of the tested cores
findings.attack: [0279] says only that the return spring 'had a two-rate characteristic' and the seat ring 'had a convoluted wall 34'. Without the number of convolutions, the spring construction and the purge-gap boundary of the tested cores, a fallback to the tested embodiment cannot be combined with any of those features without an intermediate generalisation, and the data cannot be tied to one or two convolutions.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to Example 1 the number of convolutions, the return-spring construction and the purge-gap boundary of P-1 to P-3, from the inventor's records.

findings.title: Fit band and free portion disclosed only with the relief, and tested construction not identified
findings.attack: The fit band, free portion and relief are introduced together; a claim to the first two against a plain bore is an intermediate generalisation, and [0202] disclaims the relief for the tested valve cores without saying what they had.
findings.least_narrowing_action: State whether the fit band and free portion are used with a plain core body bore, and state the construction of the tested valve cores.

findings.title: Parameters with a single value give no room to amend
findings.attack: The normal stroke, interference fit, composition, shape-setting conditions and austenite finish temperature each have one value or one bound; no relation between parameters is stated.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Ask the inventor for workable ranges, the method of determining the austenite finish temperature and any relation between dimensions; add them as candidates.

findings.title: The detent is not disclosed in combination with the other features as an alternative to the two-rate characteristic
findings.attack: Claim 6 requires 'a two-rate characteristic'; [0148] discloses a detent giving 'a step in force in place of a change of rate' once only, with no statement or combination. A detent design falls outside claim 6, and amending claim 1 to cover 'a two-rate characteristic or a detent' with the ranges, purge shoulder or seat ring draws an intermediate-generalisation objection.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a numbered statement for the detent on statement 1.3 and a sentence that the detent may replace the two-rate characteristic in each combination and with the ranges of [0238] and [0239].

findings.title: Wall-slot and valve-stem-bore arrangements too thinly described to carry an amendment
findings.attack: The wall slots are placed in a free portion and also combined with a fully retained outer surface. The valve-stem-bore arrangement is one sentence without a figure, and claim 47 excludes claim 45.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Describe the two wall-slot arrangements separately; add a figure and paragraph for the valve-stem-bore arrangement and extend claim 47 to claim 45.

findings.title: The annular purge gap bounded by the core body bore is described for the seat ring only
findings.attack: Claims 16-18 recite a purge gap 'bounded by an outer surface of the radially deflectable element and by a bore', 'a core body bore (22)', 'annular'. [0124] and [0185] describe the clearance for the seat ring 30 only; no passage describes it for the slotted sleeve, split seat ring, tapered seat ring or wiper ring, so an amendment path on a generic element lacks combination support.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add one sentence that, for each form of the radially deflectable element whose outer surface faces the core body bore, the purge gap may be an annular clearance between them.

findings.title: The fit band and relief have no numbered combination, and none with the polymer seat ring
findings.attack: Claim 26: 'the interference fit acts on a fit band (35) ... a free portion (37) which ... expands into a core body bore relief (202)'. [0186] ties the fit band to the interference fit and locating shoulder; no statement combines them, and FIG. 8 instructions exclude the fit band from the polymer seat ring. Amendment taking the relief alone, or with claims 30-31, lacks basis.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a numbered statement combining seat ring, interference fit on a fit band next to the locating shoulder, free portion and core body bore relief, and state whether it applies to the polymer seat ring 130.

findings.title: Wall slots: location and closing mechanism narrower in [0190] than in the claims
findings.attack: Claims 44 and 67 recite 'wall slots (204) ... closed at rest and open on the radial expansion'; [0190] places them 'in the free portion 37, below the sealing edge 32' with two specific closing means. An examiner may treat the unlocated slot as an intermediate generalisation, though statement 1.14 gives general basis.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a sentence that the wall slots may be at any position in the convoluted wall outside the main passage and closed at rest by any of the means described, if the inventor so conceived.

findings.title: "Closed at rest" is defined so that it has no limiting content
findings.attack: [0067] defines 'closed at rest' as the rest position of the bounding surfaces, without gas-tight closure, so every gap is 'closed' at rest. The FIG. 4A instruction draws a radial clearance at rest, which contradicts [0124]/[0187]. US 112(b): no reasonable certainty whether a permanent, widening bypass infringes. EPO/UK: G 1/24 applies the definition, widening claim 1 to read on arrangements that merely enlarge an existing clearance (e.g. US5924444A).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Redefine 'closed at rest' in [0067] functionally (bounding surfaces in contact, or spaced by no more than a stated clearance, so no substantial flow passes at rest). Exclude a clearance that already passes flow. Redraw the FIG. 4A instruction to show the contact line of [0187]. Needs the inventor's confirmation of the at-rest condition.

findings.title: Background paragraph [0007] cites a publication number that does not disclose what is attributed to it
findings.attack: The public record for US20190123456A1 is an antenna application of Alpha Wireless Ltd (https://patents.google.com/patent/US20190123456A1/en, accessed 2026-09-29), and the index records the supplied document as fictional. US: a statement in the specification that something is prior art can be used against the claims as an admission, and every cited document must be capable of being listed in an information disclosure statement. EPO: Rule 42(1)(b) requires the background art to be cited accurately. UK: an inaccurate acknowledgement is an avoidable point for an opponent.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete [0007] and check [0013]. Add nothing in its place unless a real document with saved text is identified.

findings.title: Claim 3: a product claimed by its intended use reads the same way in the US, at the EPO and in the UK
findings.attack: In all three jurisdictions a statement of purpose in a product claim limits the product to what is suitable for the purpose. Claim 3 claims a tube with an edge and a wall that is not straight, elastic; everything else describes a valve core that is not claimed. US: functional language about an unclaimed poppet gives the ring no structure, and the examiner needs only a prior ring capable of the use. EPO: the claim defines the ring by reference to another entity, a clarity objection in addition to novelty. UK: the same construction. The description acknowledges a resilient, undulating metal seat for a poppet ([0166]) and equates the load-converting geometry with a laser-cut pattern in NiTi tube ([0171]). No single embedded reference shows every feature; the objection rests on common general knowledge (A3) and is credible.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Claims 1 and 77 keep the ring in its valve core at full breadth. For the ring alone narrowing appears to be the only credible route, and it is for the human: recite structure such as the fit band and free portion of claim 66 with a continuous sealing edge. Scope given up: a loose ring without those features.

findings.title: Express definitions narrower than the claims will be applied in every forum
findings.attack: US: an applicant who defines a term is held to the definition. EPO: the description is consulted when the claims are read, and a claim that disagrees with a definition draws an Art. 84 objection. UK: the claims are read through the specification. 'Seat ring' is defined as loaded by the purge shoulder and retained in the core body, and 'purge shoulder' as a surface of the poppet. Claims 20 to 32 through claim 15 (a separate collar), claim 43 (a taper in place of the purge shoulder, [0178]), the washer of [0155] and the loose ring of claim 3 and [0162] are all outside the defined term.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Amend [0058] to refer to the load-applying surface, with the purge shoulder as the preferred example, and to a ring retained, in use, in the core body. The locked terminology row for seat ring has the same wording and needs the same correction by its owner. No claim changes.

findings.title: Inventive step: the only purpose-specific effect is not shown by the application's own data
findings.attack: The cleaning is attributed to the air purge, but [0287] reports cured sealant film on the seat-ring outer surface in the purge-gap region, and [0140]/[0289] say the test does not isolate the air purge from the snap-back wipe. The examiner recasts the problem as an alternative second flow path at a higher differential, and combines US4044791A or US5918628A (staged second opening) with US5924444A (seal deformed radially outward to open a gap, then returning), treating mechanical actuation as common general knowledge.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add disclosure explaining how the air purge acts on the purge-gap surfaces and why film remains there, plus any data separating the two cleaning actions. Otherwise reframe the stated effect around what the data show (clean sealing surfaces after 40 cycles against failures at 12-18) as the result of over-travel plus shape recovery. No claim narrowing proposed.

findings.title: Problem and solution at the EPO, nexus in the US: the data do not support the effect relied on
findings.attack: EPO: the description formulates its own technical problem at [0010] and ties the solution to the purge gap at [0013]. The inspection at [0287] found cured film on the surfaces the purge gap sweeps and clean surfaces only where the main passage runs. The examiner will say the effect is not achieved by the distinguishing feature, reformulate the problem as the provision of an alternative, and combine the acknowledged documents of [0008] and [0009]. The comparison is with unidentified valve cores ([0282]), not with the closest art. US: the longer life cannot be tied to the claimed features, so it carries little weight against a combination rejection. UK: the same facts go to obviousness and to whether the claim makes a technical contribution across its scope.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the observations the inventor actually holds: the state of the corresponding surfaces on the conventional valve cores, their identity and crack pressure, and any observation of flow through the purge gap. If the inventor confirms it, state the effect as the one the inspection supports. Add an independent fallback to the tested combination. Claim 1 is not narrowed.

findings.title: Subject matter recorded as unconfirmed candidates is drawn and claimed
findings.attack: figures.md says FIGS. 11, 12 and 13A show constructions 'not stated in the inventor's disclosure … pending inventor confirmation', and that the FIG. 4 fit band is a drafting resolution. Claims directed to subject matter that no named natural person conceived are exposed on inventorship in the US (Thaler v. Vidal), the UK ([2023] UKSC 49) and at the EPO (J 8/20).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Put each candidate to the inventor at the embodiment gate. Keep what is confirmed; delete what is not, or record its real contributor. Remove the provenance captions in every case. No narrowing if confirmed.

findings.title: Sufficiency in all three jurisdictions: the text does not say how the tested valve core opens its purge gap
findings.attack: Issue for counsel under 35 U.S.C. 112(a), Art. 83 EPC and s.14(3) of the UK Act. The gap lies between the outer surface of the ring and the bore around it and is said to open when the wall moves outward, that is, towards that bore. The description does not say which surface of the ring the purge shoulder bears on, in which direction the load acts or what reacts it, and the two places that touch the point disagree: [0113] names the upper edge, the figure instruction names the fit-band end. [0134] has the load flatten the convolution; [0172] has the equivalent bow increase under load; claim 24 depends on claim 22. Only the exit of the purge flow is described ([0194]); no inlet is identified for a ring pressed into its bore. [0202] says the fit band, free portion and relief were not the tested construction. At the EPO and in the UK an opponent needs verifiable facts to raise serious doubt, and the contradictions supply them. In the US the full scope of claims 16 to 19 rests on the one embodiment the text leaves unexplained.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the inventor's own account of the prototype before filing, when new matter is not yet a constraint: where the purge shoulder bears, the direction of the load and its reaction, the contact that closes the gap at rest, how the wall's movement opens it, where the purge flow enters and leaves, and how the tested rings were retained. Reconcile [0134] with [0172]. No claim is narrowed.

findings.title: The record of Example 1 is inconsistent with itself, which matters differently in each office
findings.attack: Forty cycles with a 24-hour hold need forty days, and the conventional valve cores' twelve to eighteen cycles need twelve to eighteen. The recorded period is nine days. US: results presented as actual, in the past tense, must be accurate, and counsel will treat an inaccurate working example as a candour issue, not a drafting one. EPO: the example is the only support for a technical effect, and evidence filed later can only build on an effect the application credibly shows. UK: the same inconsistency is available to an applicant for revocation on sufficiency and inventive step.
findings.least_narrowing_action: The inventor checks the laboratory record; the text is corrected to the record and to nothing else. If the hold was shorter for some cycles, state it and state how each leak-down figure per 24 hours was obtained.

findings.title: Added-matter exposure for the amendments most likely to be needed
findings.attack: EPO Art. 123(2) and UK s.76: the fit band and the free portion are disclosed only together with the core body bore relief ([0186], [0229]). An amendment that adds the first two without the third is an intermediate generalisation. The Summary states the first aspect with 'radial deflection' while claim 1 says 'radial expansion', so the statement of invention and the claim differ from the first day. US: the same amendments are tested as new matter under 35 U.S.C. 132 and for written description. [0249] deals properly with the ranges; the structural combinations have no equivalent.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If the inventor confirms it, add that the fit band and the free portion may be used with a plain bore and with the other retentions described, and conform [0014] to the wording of claim 1 while keeping 'radial deflection' as the stated genus.

findings.title: Breadth against one tested species, and parameters with no method of measurement
findings.attack: US: written description and enablement are judged across the full scope of the genus; one species was built and the text says the ranges are the inventors' belief. EPO: a parameter in a claim needs a method of measurement in the claim or the description; none is given for the crack pressure, the over-travel differential, the purge gap width inside an assembled valve core or the austenite finish temperature, and the over-travel differential depends on a flow that was not recorded. UK: the claim must be workable across its breadth without research, and the PEEK ring of claims 30, 31, 74 and 75 is claimed although the description cannot say it would open the gap. The art is mechanical and fairly predictable, which keeps this at medium.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the methods by which the prototype values were measured or set, and the design reasoning the inventor has for the untested forms. Keep the statements of what was not tested. Nothing is narrowed.

findings.title: Claim format and fees: multiple dependencies, claim count and two-part form
findings.attack: US: 45 of the 86 claims are multiple dependent and 37 of them depend on another multiple dependent claim, which 37 CFR 1.75(c) does not allow; such claims are objected to and not examined, a surcharge applies, and for fees each multiple dependent claim counts as the number of claims it refers to, several hundred here. EPO: the form is accepted, claims fees run from the sixteenth claim, claim 1 is not in the two-part form of Rule 43(1), and 86 claims invite a conciseness objection. UK: the form is accepted; excess-claims and excess-pages fees apply to a text of this length. In all three, claims 38 and 50 limit a product by air flow, sealant and a tyre chamber that are not part of it.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Prepare a US claim set with single dependencies on the chains that matter. For the EPO and the UK keep the set and let counsel decide the count against the fees. Recast claim 50 as a tyre chamber fitted with the tyre valve and containing sealant, with basis at [0327].

findings.title: Claims 45, 49 and 50 are defined by, or contradict, entities outside the claimed category
findings.attack: Claim 45 bounds the purge gap of a valve core by a valve stem that the valve core does not contain. Claim 49 ('formed in the valve stem') contradicts claim 47 ('received in a bore of the valve stem'). Claim 50 defines a tyre valve by the sealant in the tube. US 112(b)/(d); EPO Art 84.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Move claim 45 under claim 47. Amend claim 47 to 'received in, or formed in, the valve stem'. Recast claim 50 as a tyre-chamber claim, following statement 2.5 in [0327].

findings.title: Definiteness of 'closed at rest' under the US, EPO and UK standards
findings.attack: [0067] makes 'closed' mean 'unloaded', and FIG. 4A is to show a clearance at rest. US: the claim must tell the skilled person its scope with reasonable certainty, and a closed gap that may be open does not. EPO: Art. 84. UK: s.14(5)(b). The same definition lets the claim read on a clearance that merely widens, which is a novelty exposure as well.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a positive test to [0067] that the inventor can confirm, for example no flow path through the purge gap from the upstream side to the tyre chamber at rest. Correct or explain the FIG. 4A clearance. No claim changes.

findings.title: Drawings: claimed features not shown, figure and numerals not described, text on the sheets
findings.attack: US: 37 CFR 1.83(a) requires the drawings to show every feature claimed; no figure shows the collar of claim 15, the spring constructions of claims 9 and 10 or the valve stem bore of claim 45. Reference characters must appear in both drawing and description: 220, 402 and 404 do not, and FIG. 13A has no brief description. EPO: Rule 46(2) keeps text off the drawings except where indispensable and requires the reference signs to match the description; the status captions prescribed for FIGS. 10 to 13 offend the first and 220, 402 and 404 the second. UK: the same requirements under the Patents Rules. The figure files also contain process notes that are not filing text.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add figures for the claimed collar, spring constructions and valve stem bore. Describe FIG. 13A and 220 or remove both. Register 402 and 404 or drop them. Take the status captions off the drawings and strip the process notes.

findings.title: Drawings: FIG. 13A undescribed, numerals missing from the description, text legends in captions
findings.attack: FIG. 13A and numeral 220 are absent from the description (37 CFR 1.74; Rule 42(1)(d) EPC). Numeral 146, used in claim 1, is absent from the description. Captions such as 'Candidate … not built or tested' are non-indispensable text in drawings (Rule 46(2)(f) EPC) and put the provenance problem on the face of the patent.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Describe FIG. 13A once it is confirmed, or drop it and renumber FIG. 13B. Introduce numeral 146 in [0181]-[0182]. Reduce captions to view titles.

findings.title: Functional claiming: US means-plus-function exposure and EPO essential features
findings.attack: US: 'element' and 'surface' qualified only by function invite construction under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), which confines the term to the structures described and their equivalents; [0106] says much the same in the applicant's own words. EPO: claim 1 defines the purge gap by the result to be achieved and omits what the description shows to be needed for the result in a pressed-in ring, namely a portion left free to move ([0186] to [0188]); an essential-features objection under Art. 84 is to be expected. UK: support under s.14(5)(c) is judged against the same breadth.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reword [0106] to cover any structure that performs the function, including those described. Add a sentence, if the inventor confirms it, that a free portion can be provided with any of the retentions described, so that the feature is available as an amendment without being essential to claim 1. No claim changes now.

findings.title: Functional genus terms invite a US 112(f) construction
findings.attack: 'Radially deflectable element', 'return bias' and 'load-converting geometry' are generic nouns defined by function, and [0106] says each covers 'each structure described herein that performs the function'. A US court may apply 112(f), limiting each term to the disclosed structures and equivalents, with an indefiniteness risk if the linkage is unclear.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Give each term structural content that avoids 112(f) without narrowing the genus (e.g. 'having a wall that bounds the purge gap'; 'comprising at least one spring'). State the linked structures expressly in [0106]. Counsel may instead accept the 112(f) reading in the US.

findings.title: Method claim 2 is performed by the rider; enforcement against a supplier is indirect in every jurisdiction
findings.attack: The person who performs claim 2 is the cyclist with a pump. UK and the EPC states exempt private, non-commercial use, so the supplier is reached only as a contributory infringer who supplies means relating to an essential element with the required knowledge. US: there is no private-use exemption, but the supplier is reached only through inducement or contributory infringement, each with a knowledge requirement and each needing proof that a user actually reached the over-travel. A competitor who supplies no instructions, or a spring whose over-travel differential ordinary pumping rarely reaches, weakens that proof. The product claims carry the enforcement, and claim 3 is the weak one (F-30-5).
findings.least_narrowing_action: No change to claim 2. Secure the product claims first. Counsel may consider a claim to the valve core in a package with instructions, for which [0276] is basis, where the jurisdiction gives such a claim weight.

findings.title: Second independent valve-core claim (claim 77), unity a posteriori, and US restriction
findings.attack: Claim 77 is a second independent valve-core claim outside claim 1's scope (EPO Rule 43(2)). If claim 3 is read as a bare undulating tubular ring, claims 1-2 and 3-4 share no special technical feature (Art 82). In the US, restriction among claims 1, 2, 3 and 4 is likely.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recast claim 77 as dependent on claim 20 via the seat ring of claim 3, or delete it. Keep claim 3's special technical feature aligned with claim 1 (see F-32-2). Budget for a possible US divisional.

findings.title: Sufficiency across the breadth of the genus claims
findings.attack: Only the NiTi convoluted seat ring has been built. [0210] says spring-tempered metal 'is not proposed for a continuous convoluted wall', yet claims 20-26 have no material limit. [0290] gives no purge gap width for PEEK. UK breadth-of-claim sufficiency, EPO Art 83 serious doubts from the application's own words, and US Wands factors.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add disclosure within the inventor's conception on material suitability per form, with an estimated PEEK strain and recovery. Recast the [0210] exclusion as guidance by required recoverable strain. Narrowing claims 20-26 by material is the last resort and would give up non-NiTi metal seat rings.

findings.title: Unity, restriction and embodiments that no claim covers
findings.attack: EPO: Rule 43(2) and Art. 82. Claims 1 and 77 are two valve cores of different scope, and if claim 3 is not new the seat ring group shares no special technical feature with the valve core group. Embodiments outside the claims (the thermal variant, the disc-spring form of [0179], Statement 7.1) must be marked as such or removed before grant, and the numbered statements at [0297] to [0348] are claim-like clauses in the description. The thermal variant also uses 'purge gap' against the definition at [0065]. US: restriction between the valve core, the method of use, the seat ring and its manufacture is to be expected, and what is described but not claimed is exposed to dedication. UK: plurality of invention under s.14(5)(d), with the same divisional planning.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete nothing. Present the thermal variant as a separate aspect and word [0065] 'in the first aspect'. Recast the numbered statements as numbered embodiments in prose, because they are basis for amendment. Counsel plans divisionals for the seat ring with its manufacture and for the thermal variant.

findings.title: US multiple-dependency form and claims fees in all three offices
findings.attack: US: a multiple dependent claim may not rest on another multiple dependent claim (35 USC 112(e), 37 CFR 1.75(c)); claims such as 13 (via claim 11) and 86 (via 65-69) are improper and would not be examined; proper ones attract a surcharge. EPO: claims fees for claims 16-50, higher from 51 (Rule 45). UK: excess-claims fee over 25. 86 claims are filed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Prepare a US claim set with single dependencies that keeps the chosen fallback chains. For the EPO and UK, consolidate range and material fallbacks that already have description basis in [0240]-[0249].

findings.title: Approximate and nominal values in claims
findings.attack: 'About 0.03 mm' and 'nominal composition' invite an EPO clarity objection. [0056] defines 'about' by tolerance but gives no figure.
findings.least_narrowing_action: State a tolerance in [0250]/[0259] if the inventor has one, or delete 'about' and 'nominal' in the European claim set.

findings.title: Characterisations of the prior art and of the problem are required at the EPO and costly in the US
findings.attack: EPO: Rule 42(1)(c) expects the problem and solution to be stated, and the text does so. US: the same sentences are read as admissions about the art and as statements of what the invention is, which narrow the claims in litigation; [0013], [0015] and [0166] are the clearest. One text cannot serve both practices without a choice. 'Presta-pattern' is used without a standard or a definition, and the dates of the test appear in the description ([0283]), which fixes a date of reduction to practice on the public record for no benefit.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Counsel chooses per jurisdiction. For a US text, confine each statement about a document to what it says and recast [0015] as embodiment language. Define 'Presta-pattern' by its dimensions or a standard. Consider removing the test dates once the record is reconciled (F-30-2).

findings.title: Relative orientation terms without a frame of reference
findings.attack: 'Below' and 'upper' have no reference when every axial view is drawn with the valve axis horizontal. [0117] glosses 'below' as spacing along the axis, but claim 14 does not use the gloss.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Claim 14: replace 'located below the sealing face' with 'spaced from the sealing face along the axis of the poppet'. Define 'upper' in [0112] by the pump-head or tyre-chamber side.

findings.title: Claim 3 claims the seat ring alone and is limited only by an intended use
findings.attack: The structure claimed is a tube, an edge at one end, a wall that is not straight, and elasticity. The poppet, the load-applying surface, the normal stroke, the over-travel, the main passage and the purge gap all belong to a valve core that claim 3 does not claim; they state what the ring is for and limit it only to suitability. The examiner reads the claim on any resilient tubular element of suitable size whose wall is not straight. The description itself equates the load-converting geometry with a zig-zag or diamond-cell pattern laser-cut in NiTi tube ([0171]); a tubular resilient metal seat engaged by a poppet, with undulating portions, is in US11549591B1, which [0166] acknowledges. No single embedded reference shows every feature, so the objection is put on common general knowledge (A3) for novelty and, failing that, on inventive step, together with a clarity objection that the ring is defined by parts it does not contain. If claim 3 falls, claims 4 and 78 to 83 add only the ordinary process chain for NiTi tube (US9126251B2) and claims 70 to 75 add known materials.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Breadth is kept where it is defensible: claim 1 and claim 77 claim the ring in its valve core. For the ring alone, narrowing appears to be the only credible route, and the human should decide it: recite structure that a known tube would not have for another reason, for example the fit band and the free portion of claim 66 with a continuous sealing edge. Scope given up: a loose ring without those features, which would then be reached only through claim 77 and indirect infringement.

findings.title: Claim 3 seat ring is distinguished from undulating tubular metal seats only by its intended use
findings.attack: The poppet, over-travel and purge gap are not part of the claimed article. What remains is a tubular ring with a sealing edge at one end and a wall that grows radially under axial load and recovers. US11549591B1 FIG. 10 shows a resilient metal seat element 812 with a cylindrical sidewall 814 and undulating flanges forming the seat for poppet 804; under [0061] a wall not straight in section is 'convoluted'. US: intended use does not distinguish a capable structure. EPO/UK: 'for' means suitable for; EP3171056A1 (wave-section ring whose flattening moves it radially) supplies the conversion. Claims 4 and 86 (standard NiTi shape-setting, US9126251B2) and 62-64 fall with it.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to claim 3 that the wall's outer surface, with a bore surrounding the seat ring, bounds the purge gap (claim 65, [0124], statement 4.1), and that the load-converting geometry lies between the sealing edge and the opposite end ([0167]). The through-wall purge of claim 67 then needs its own route.

findings.title: Every independent claim requires a contact-free first range of travel
findings.attack: Claims 1 and 2 require a normal stroke in which the surface is spaced from the element and the purge gap is closed; claim 3 requires an over-travel beyond a normal stroke. A competitor lets the load-applying surface rest on the deflectable element when the valve is closed, so that the element deflects and the second flow path opens progressively from the first movement of the poppet. There is then no normal stroke as defined in [0071] and no literal infringement of any claim. It works commercially: a single-rate spring, no threshold to tune, and a purge on every inflation whatever the pump delivers. With a rigid seat and a separate ring the seal is unaffected. [0015] and [0072] make the two ranges essential in the applicant's own words, which blocks equivalents and blocks later broadening. This is a negative limitation on internal behaviour in an independent claim.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If it is within the inventor's conception, add an embodiment in which the load-applying surface bears on the deflectable element from the start of the lift, and an independent claim without the spaced-throughout and closed-throughout limitations; keep those limitations as a dependent claim; recast [0015] as embodiment language. If it is not within the conception, this stays as a residual risk for the human.

findings.title: Example 1 cannot have been run as recorded: forty 24-hour cycles in a nine-day test
findings.attack: One inflation cycle includes a hold of 24 hours. Forty cycles need at least forty days; the eighteen, fourteen and twelve cycles of the conventional valve cores need eighteen, fourteen and twelve. The recorded test period is nine days. The leak-down figures are each stated per 24 hours, so the hold cannot simply be read out. The dates, the hold period or the cycle counts are wrong. Example 1 is the only data in the application, it is presented as an actual example in [0278], and the Background and the Technical problem rely on it at [0003] and [0012]. An examiner gives the example no weight; an opponent uses the inconsistency to discredit every effect the application asserts; in the US the accuracy of results reported as actual is a matter counsel must clear before filing.
findings.least_narrowing_action: The inventor checks the laboratory record and states which of the three is correct. The text is then corrected to the record and to nothing else. If some holds were shorter than 24 hours, say so and state how each leak-down figure per 24 hours was obtained. No value is to be adjusted without the record.

findings.title: Inventive step: the application's own inspection contradicts the effect attributed to the purge gap
findings.attack: Closest art: the conventional tyre valve core of [0003], a spring-biased poppet on a seat in a threaded core body. Claim 1 differs by the over-travel in which a surface moved by the poppet deforms an element to open a second flow path. The effect relied on, at [0010] and [0013], is that air through the purge gap removes sealant film from the surfaces it sweeps. The inspection at [0287] found cured film on exactly those surfaces after forty cycles. The surfaces found clean, the sealing edge and the sealing face, bound the main passage, where by [0011] the ordinary stream of air already flows. The comparison cannot attribute the longer life to the purge gap either: the conventional valve cores are unidentified ([0282]), their crack pressure, seat material and seat geometry are not given, and [0289] concedes that the two cleaning actions were never separated. With no effect shown for the distinguishing feature, the problem falls to providing a second flow path that opens at a higher pressure differential. Staged opening by further poppet travel is acknowledged at [0008] and shown in US4044791A; a ring that deforms radially outward to open a gap and returns when the valve closes is acknowledged at [0009] and shown in US5924444A, a valve for mounting on a tyre valve stem; cleaning a valve seat with air through an annular slit is in US3570510A. No embedded reference deforms the ring by a surface moved by the poppet; the examiner will call that a mechanical alternative to deformation by flow. The objection is credible against claims 1, 2 and 3 and against claims 38 and 57, which recite the air purge itself.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add what the inventor actually recorded: the state of the same surfaces on the conventional valve cores at failure, the identity and crack pressure of those valve cores, and any observation that air passed through the purge gap. If the inventor confirms it, restate [0010] and [0013] so that the effect asserted is the one the inspection supports, namely that the surfaces on which the poppet seals stay free of sealant film. Add, without touching claim 1, an independent fallback to the tested combination (claim 1 with claims 20 and 27), so that one claim rests on the example as run. No narrowing of claim 1 is proposed.

findings.title: Principal embodiment: how the purge gap opens, and how air reaches it, is not disclosed and the stated geometry contradicts itself
findings.attack: Five gaps, each on the face of the text. (1) Direction. The purge gap lies between the outer surface of the ring and the bore around it, and is said to open when the wall moves outward. An outer surface that moves outward moves towards the bore that bounds the gap. The text never says which contact closes the gap at rest, or why an outward movement breaks that contact instead of tightening it. (2) Load path. The description does not say which surface of the seat ring the purge shoulder bears on, in which axial direction the load acts, or what reacts it. [0113] puts the load at the upper edge, which is the sealing edge that the sealing face has just left; the figure instruction puts the purge shoulder at the fit-band end, which is the end pressed into the bore and seated on the locating shoulder, where a load passes into the core body without crossing the convoluted wall. (3) Sign of the deformation. [0134], [0170] and claim 22 have the axial load flatten the convolution; [0172] says that a single outward bow, which it equates with one convolution, increases under axial load. Claim 24 claims the single outward bow in dependence on claim 22, so one claim requires the bow to flatten while the description says it grows. (4) Inlet. Only the exit of the purge flow is described. With the outer surface of the ring pressed into the bore, no route is identified by which air at pump pressure enters the gap from upstream without passing the sealing edge. (5) As built. [0202] states that the fit band, the free portion and the core body bore relief are not the tested construction, so the construction that did run for forty cycles is not described in the one respect that matters. An examiner puts this as lack of enablement of the only tested embodiment and of claims 16 to 19, 45, 58 and 65; an opponent uses the contradiction as the verifiable fact that raises serious doubt.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add disclosure taken from the inventor's prototype and drawings: the surface of the seat ring on which the purge shoulder bears and the direction of the load; the support that reacts it; the contact that closes the purge gap at rest and how the movement of the wall opens it; the entry and the exit of the purge flow; and the retention actually used in the tested valve cores. Reconcile [0134], [0170] and [0172], and claim 24 with claim 22. No claim is narrowed. If the inventor's answer is that part of the wall moves inward to open the gap, claims 1 to 3 need the genus wording 'radial deflection', which [0014] already uses.

findings.title: The axial and face-gap forms are described, stated not to be a radial expansion, and claimed nowhere
findings.attack: [0179] teaches a working alternative: a disc spring whose rim seals on a face, flattened by the load-applying surface in over-travel so that a purge gap opens at the face. The description then says in terms that this is not a radial expansion. Every independent claim requires a radial expansion of a radially deflectable element. A competitor builds [0179]: a catalogue disc spring, no NiTi, no shape-setting, and by [0179] the same part supplies the second spring stage. The product sells on the same promise, a second flow path opened by over-travel. Subject matter described and left unclaimed is open to the argument that it was given to the public, and an equivalents case has to overcome the applicant's own sentence.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent claim, or broaden claim 1 and move radial expansion to a dependent claim, to a deflectable element whose deflection by the load-applying surface in the over-travel opens the purge gap, on the basis of [0179] and [0180]. Add a figure for the disc-spring form, since none exists, and conform [0014]. Nothing is narrowed.

findings.title: The Background attributes a valve core to a publication number that belongs to an antenna application
findings.attack: The prior-art index records the document supplied under this number as fictional and not fetched. The public record for US20190123456A1 is 'Multiple-input multiple-output (mimo) omnidirectional antenna', Alpha Wireless Ltd (https://patents.google.com/patent/US20190123456A1/en, accessed 2026-09-29). As drafted, the Background cites a document that does not say what is attributed to it, and admits as prior art an enlarged bore, a fluoropolymer-coated sealing face, a rigid seat and a removable insert for sealant deposits. 'In the documents referred to above' in [0013] sweeps it in. An examiner may hold the applicant to the admission; an opponent will.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete [0007] and check that no other passage relies on it. Put nothing in its place unless a real document with saved text is identified.

findings.title: The definitions of seat ring and purge shoulder contradict claims 3, 15 with 20, 43 and 77
findings.attack: [0050] applies the definitions to the claims. A seat ring is defined as loaded by the purge shoulder and as retained in the core body, and the purge shoulder is defined as a surface of the poppet. Claims 20 to 32 depend through claim 15, where the load comes from a separate collar. Claim 43 claims a tapered seat ring loaded by a taper that [0178] says replaces the purge shoulder. Claim 3 claims a ring not yet in any core body, and [0162] says it is supplied loose. On the applicant's own lexicon none of these is a seat ring. The examiner objects that the claims and the description disagree. A defendant whose ring is loaded by a collar or a washer, or who sells loose rings, argues that it has no seat ring as the patent defines one.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Amend [0058] to refer to the load-applying surface, with the purge shoulder as the preferred example, and to a ring 'retained, in use, in the core body'. [0063] can stay. The row for seat ring in the locked terminology carries the same purge-shoulder wording and should be corrected by its owner. No claim changes and nothing is narrowed.

findings.title: [0106] ties the functional terms to the structures described
findings.attack: 'Radially deflectable element', 'load-applying surface', 'return bias' and 'load-converting geometry' carry little structure of their own. [0106] says they cover each structure described. That is the scope a means-plus-function construction would give in the US, and in any forum it invites the argument that a structure not described is outside the term.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reword [0106] to 'covers any structure that performs the function, including each structure described herein'. No claim changes.

findings.title: Categorical statements exclude any opening by pressure or flow
findings.attack: The description defines the invention against a flow path opened by pressure or flow. A competitor fits a resilient ring or sleeve that the pressure differential itself expands above a threshold: no load-applying surface, no purge shoulder, no two-rate spring, and the same second flow path at high pump pressure. It does not infringe literally, and the applicant's own sentences answer an equivalents case. These statements are also what separates claim 1 from US5924444A, so they cannot simply be removed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Keep claim 1. Recast [0016] and [0135] as statements about the embodiments described, and confine [0013] to what each document says. If the inventor has conceived an opening assisted by pressure in addition to the mechanical load, add it as an embodiment.

findings.title: FIG. 5 places both thresholds at the wrong end of their ranges
findings.attack: The figure marks the crack pressure at the end of the normal stroke and the over-travel differential at the end of the over-travel. [0069] and [0070] put each at the start of its range. A curve drawn from the origin shows no preload, so nothing holds the poppet closed until a crack pressure is reached. The drawing contradicts the definitions on which claims 5, 6 and 11 rest.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Correct the figure instruction: the curve starts at zero travel at the force that corresponds to the crack pressure, and the over-travel differential is marked at the change of slope.

findings.title: Figures and registry carry a figure, numerals and status captions that the description does not
findings.attack: FIG. 13A and numeral 220 are in the figure set and the registry but not in the description, which lists FIG. 13B alone. Numerals 402 and 404 are called for on FIG. 5 and appear in neither the registry table nor the description. The captions for FIGS. 10 to 13 put statements of status on the drawing sheets. No figure shows the collar of claim 15, the springs of claims 9 and 10 or the valve stem bore of claim 45, and the US requires the drawings to show every claimed feature. The figure plan in the package records that the constructions of FIGS. 11, 12 and 13A were not in the inventor's disclosure and await confirmation, yet claims 26, 40 to 44 and 67 claim them. The figure files also carry process notes, such as references to the inventor's sketch files and to claim strategy, which are not filing text and which a blind package should not contain.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Describe FIG. 13A and numeral 220 in the description or remove both, renumbering FIG. 13B if FIG. 13A goes. Register 402 and 404 or drop them. Take the status captions off the drawings; the description already says what was built. Add figures for the claimed collar, spring constructions and valve stem bore. Strip the process notes. Whether the constructions of claims 26, 40 to 44 and 67 are confirmed as the inventor's is for the human (Q2).

findings.title: Method claim 2 is performed by the end user
findings.attack: Every step of claim 2 is performed by the cyclist with a pump; the competitor manufacturer is at most an indirect infringer (US inducement or contributory infringement, UK s60(2), national indirect infringement in EPC states), and the steps occur only when the user reaches the over-travel differential ([0273]). Proof of user conduct and of knowledge is hard, and direct infringers are individual consumers.
findings.least_narrowing_action: None to claim 2. Rely on claims 1, 3 and 47. Counsel may consider a valve core supplied with over-travel inflation instructions ([0276]), subject to printed-matter limits.

findings.title: Normal stroke and over-travel are defined by the contact itself, so claim 1 has no independent travel limitation
findings.attack: [0071]/[0072] define the boundary as the first contact, so 'spaced … throughout the normal stroke' is true by definition. Claim 1 is not tied to the two thresholds of claim 5 and reads on a single-rate poppet that at full lift pushes a compliant element opening a bypass, which eases the F-32-1 combination.
findings.least_narrowing_action: In [0071], also mark the end of the normal stroke by an independent structural feature (change of rate [0122] or stop [0151]). Fallback: fold claim 5 into claim 1. That is narrowing; it gives up travel not produced by a separate over-travel differential.

findings.title: One species built; the polymer, spring-metal and other forms are claimed on expectation
findings.attack: One form has been built. Claims 30, 31, 74 and 75 claim a PEEK ring of the prototype geometry although the description cannot say that such a ring would open the purge gap at all. The genus of claim 1 runs from a polymer to spring steel. In the US the question is whether the inventor had possession of the genus; at the EPO and in the UK it is whether the claim can be worked across its width without research. The candour of the text is to the applicant's credit, and each candid sentence is also an admission.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the design reasoning the inventor has, for example the strain in PEEK at the stated convolution amplitude and why the bending-dominated forms stay elastic. Keep the statements of what was not tested. Nothing is narrowed.

findings.title: Principal-embodiment geometry: axial load path and purge-flow route are not stated consistently
findings.attack: A purge shoulder on the poppet can reach the seat ring only at the end away from the sealing edge, which is the retained fit-band end (as the FIG. 2 instruction says), whereas [0113] says the load is applied 'at its upper edge', the sealing edge. The text does not say what reacts the load so that it passes through the convoluted wall, nor how pump-side air enters an annular gap closed on one side by the interference-fitted fit band. On the text alone this raises 112(a)/Art 83 doubts about the only built embodiment, and 112(b)/Art 84 points on 'upper' and 'below'.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an inventor-confirmed paragraph stating the seat-ring orientation, the side and end the purge shoulder contacts, what reacts the axial load, and the purge-gap inlet and outlet. Align [0113] and the FIG. 2 instruction.

findings.title: Snap-back wipe: the ring recovers while the sealing face is a full normal stroke away
findings.attack: By [0137] the ring recovers when the purge shoulder lifts, and only then does the poppet return through the normal stroke, which was 0.6 mm in the prototype ([0235]). At the moment of recovery the sealing face is not touching the ring. How the ring moves across that face and shears film from it is not disclosed; [0138] offers a belief. Claims 32, 56 and 76 recite it as fact.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the inventor's account of which surfaces touch during the recovery and when. If there is none, recast claims 32, 56 and 76 to what is disclosed: the ring recovers its shape at the sealing edge before the sealing face seats again.

findings.title: The actuating condition and the claimed values cannot be reproduced or checked from the text
findings.attack: The over-travel differential is a pressure difference across a poppet that is already open, so it depends on the flow delivered, which was not recorded. That the poppet reached the over-travel, and that the gap opened to 0.15 mm, rests on a sound heard when the pump head was removed. No method is given for measuring the crack pressure, the over-travel differential, the purge gap width inside an assembled valve core, or the austenite finish temperature, which is a supplier's specification. Claims 11, 12, 19, 29, 33, 34, 53 and 72 recite these values. A third party cannot tell whether it is inside them and the proprietor cannot prove that anyone is.
findings.least_narrowing_action: State how each value was measured or set in the prototype, and the method for the austenite finish temperature. Where a value is a design value and not a measurement, say so.

findings.title: The fallback ladder adds conventional features and untested ranges
findings.attack: If claim 1 falls, most fallbacks do not rescue it. Claims 5 to 10 add return springs of ordinary two-stage kinds (A2). Claims 11, 12, 19, 33, 34, 68 and 69 add ranges for which [0230] disclaims any tested effect, so the examiner treats them as arbitrary. Claims 27 to 29 and 70 to 73 add a superelastic NiTi seat, a seat material already used in valves (US6019118A). Claims 35 to 37 add two materials and a lock nut that the description calls conventional. Claims 4 and 78 to 83 add the usual route for NiTi tube. The claims with structure peculiar to the invention are 20 to 26 and 40 to 44, and those are the untested forms.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete nothing. For each fallback that matters, state in the description the technical reason that ties the feature to the opening of the purge gap; some exist already at [0149] and [0188]. Add a mid-level independent fallback that combines claim 1 with claims 20, 21 and 25.

findings.title: The thermal variant uses 'purge gap' against its own definition, and unclaimed numbered statements remain
findings.attack: A purge gap as defined is opened in the over-travel by the load-applying surface. The thermal variant opens 'the purge gap' by warming, with the poppet seated. A defined term is used against its definition. The thermal variant, Statement 7.1 (a wiper ring with no purge gap), Statement 5.6 and Statements 2.5 and 2.6 fall outside every claim: the EPO will require the description brought into line, and in the US what is described and unclaimed is exposed. The numbered statements at [0297] to [0348] read as claims inside the description, which the EPO objects to before grant.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Present the thermal variant as a separate aspect outside the first aspect and word [0065] 'in the first aspect'. Counsel decides whether to claim it separately or in a divisional. Recast the numbered statements as numbered embodiments in prose; do not delete them, because they are basis for amendment.

findings.title: The two-piece seat is not described as opening a purge gap
findings.attack: The two-piece seat text says only that the wiper ring 144 is deflected outward and wipes. No purge gap, location or air route is described, numeral 146 (claim 1) is absent from the description, and nothing explains how the purge shoulder passes the rigid seat 140 on which the same poppet seals. US written description of this species under claim 1; EPO reference signs pointing to an undescribed feature.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0181]-[0182] the purge gap 146 between wiper ring 144 and core body bore 22, its closure at rest and opening, its air route into the tyre chamber 80, and how the purge shoulder reaches the wiper ring past the rigid seat. Inventor to confirm.

findings.title: Convolution amplitude claimed where no convolution is required
findings.attack: Through claim 3 the geometry may be a strut pattern or helical slot with no convolution, leaving the amplitude alternative without a referent.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Limit the amplitude alternative of claim 68, and claim 69, to dependency on claims 62-67; keep the other dimensions on claim 3.

findings.title: Four categories and two valve cores of different scope
findings.attack: The set claims a valve core, a method of use, a seat ring and a method of making it, and a second valve core in claim 77 that recites no load-applying surface. If claim 3 is not new (F-32-4), the seat ring group, claims 3, 4 and 62 to 86, shares no special technical feature with the valve core group. A US restriction between the four groups is to be expected. Claim 77 introduces 'a valve core' and 'a poppet' that claim 3 has already introduced, so it is unclear whether they are the same parts.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete nothing. Plan for a divisional on the seat ring and its manufacture. In claim 77 say that the poppet is the poppet whose sealing face seats on the sealing edge of the seat ring.

findings.title: Multiple dependencies, a colliding term in claim 42, and claims limited by things outside the claimed product
findings.attack: Forty-five of the 86 claims are multiple dependent, and 37 of those depend on another multiple dependent claim, from claim 13 onward. The US does not accept that form, and counted the US way the set runs to several hundred claims. 'Split seat' is a locked synonym of the two-piece seat, so 'split seat ring' in claim 42 and [0177] can be read as the two-piece seat; `pc terms` flags it on the claims. Claim 50 limits a tyre valve by a tyre chamber and by sealant, neither of which is part of the valve claimed, and claim 38 defines the valve core by an air flow and a sealant film that exist only in use.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Prepare a US claim set with single dependencies on the chains that matter. Declare 'split seat ring' as a new term, or rename it, and take 'split seat' out of the synonyms of the two-piece seat. Recast claim 50 as a tyre chamber fitted with the tyre valve and containing sealant, for which Statement 2.5 at [0327] is basis.

findings.title: Purge gap width range is claimed for every radially deflectable element
findings.attack: [0237] states the range for the seat-ring purge gap 60 and ties it to flattening of convolution 36. Claim 19, through claim 16, applies it to the slotted sleeve, split and tapered rings and wiper ring, which have no stated width. A US written-description question and an intermediate-generalisation risk for EPO amendments.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If the inventor agrees, state in [0237] that the range applies to any radially deflectable element. Otherwise make claim 19 depend on claims 20-26.

findings.title: Axially deflecting and tilting elements are described but lie outside every claim
findings.attack: [0179] describes a disc spring whose rim lifts from a face and states that its deflection is not a radial expansion. All independent claims recite a radial expansion. The alternative is disclosed, unclaimed and expressly distinguished, so equivalents are unlikely to recover it, and the part is cheaper than a seat ring of NiTi alloy.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent claim, or broaden claim 1, to recite a deflectable element and a deflection that opens the purge gap, with radial expansion in a dependent claim. Basis [0179], [0180].

findings.title: Axially deflecting element taught in [0179]-[0180] avoids 'radially deflectable element' and 'radial expansion'
findings.attack: Claim 1 requires 'a radially deflectable element' and 'a radial expansion'. [0179] discloses a conical disc spring whose rim lifts axially to open a purge gap at a face and states that its deflection 'is not a radial expansion'; [0180] adds axial and tilting deformations. The disc spring also provides the second spring stage, so it is a cheaper one-part design that the specification teaches but claims 1 and 2 exclude (dedication to the public in the US; weak equivalents position in EPO/UK).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a separate independent valve-core claim (and matching method claim) reciting 'a deflectable element' whose deflection by the load-applying surface in the over-travel opens the purge gap, with the other claim 1 limitations unchanged; support [0179], [0180], [0081], [0065]. Keep claim 1 unchanged because the broader claim is closer to US4044791A (INDEX #2).

findings.title: Contact from lift-off avoids 'spaced ... throughout the normal stroke'
findings.attack: The normal stroke ends where the load-applying surface first meets the element ([0071]) and the over-travel is the travel in which, and only in which, it bears on the element ([0072]). A competitor sets the collar at zero clearance or light contact from lift-off and makes the purge gap open only above a load threshold (stiffer convolution, detent). The commercial effect is kept but no travel exists in which the surface is spaced from the element, so claim 1 is not literally met, and [0015] presents the spacing as essential, weakening equivalents.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a parallel claim bounding the travel ranges by pressure and gap state: purge gap closed while the pressure differential is between the crack pressure and the over-travel differential and opened when it exceeds the over-travel differential ([0071] last sentence, [0120], [0132], [0239]); this needs a disclosed embodiment in which the load-applying surface contacts or preloads the element through the normal stroke and the gap opens only above a load threshold, if within the inventor's conception.

findings.title: No independent claim covers cleaning by deflection of the seat without a secondary flow path
findings.attack: Every independent claim requires a purge gap that is a secondary flow path. [0064] and [0126] state that a flow path enlarged by deflection of the seat remains the main passage. [0287] reports clean sealing surfaces and cured sealant film on the purge gap surface. A competitor keeps the over-travel and a seat that deflects and recovers, removes the purge gap, and is outside all 86 claims while keeping the cleaning action that the inspection result is consistent with.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent claim to a valve core in which the over-travel load deflects the element and the shape recovery moves the element across the sealing face, with no purge gap recited. Basis for the two-piece seat at [0182], [0294], [0347]; the one-piece seat ring needs a statement from the inventors. No existing claim is narrowed.

findings.title: 'Load-converting geometry' at risk of US 112(f) structure-limited construction; no strut-pattern or helical-slot dependents
findings.attack: 'a wall having a load-converting geometry' is defined only by function ([0104], [0106]). A US court may treat 'geometry' as a nonce term under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), confining the claim to disclosed structures and equivalents, with indefiniteness risk if the link to structure is found unclear. The seat ring dependents name only the convoluted wall (62-64) and wall slots (67), leaving strut-pattern and helical-slot rings without a named fallback.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add dependent claims to claim 3 and in the claim 21 family: 'wherein the load-converting geometry is a strut pattern cut in the wall' ([0171]) and 'wherein the load-converting geometry is a helical slot through the wall' ([0173]).

findings.title: A valve core sold alone escapes where the bore of the valve stem bounds the purge gap
findings.attack: Claim 1 recites the opening of the purge gap without the conditional wording that claim 3 uses. Where the gap forms against the bore of the valve stem, a valve core sold alone opens no gap, and the manufacturer is at most an indirect infringer.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to claim 45 and to a new dependent claim the wording that the valve core is configured so that, when fitted in a valve stem, the radial expansion opens the purge gap against a bore of the valve stem. Basis [0125], [0189], [0161].

findings.title: An element loaded otherwise than by a surface moved by the poppet, or a rigid sliding element, is outside the claims
